newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: C.BANK SETS RULES FOR TERM DEPOSIT AUCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: C.BANK SETS RULES FOR TERM DEPOSIT AUCTIONS.

text.p: The Lithuanian central bank said on Thursday that its weekly board meeting had decided on the rules to launch term deposit auctions.
"The auctions for term deposits will...allow the Bank of Lithuania to regulate the surplus liquidity in the banking system," the central bank said in a statement.
"Together with repo rules, these term deposit auctions will give the central bank more opportunities...to influence money markets," the statement said.
"If banks have excess liquidity, the central bank will deposit the money for a fixed term," Gitanas Nauseda, the head of the central bank's policy department, told Reuters.
"Banks currently have excess liqudity and so they require this service at the moment," he said.
He did not say exactly when the the central bank would start taking the deposits.
He added that the repo auctions would begin in two to three weeks' time, depending on market circumstances.
